D1.text: Every user-visible error is exactly one `line N: <message>` line, no traceback

D2.text: Evaluator is iterative for calls/blocks: user nesting depth never becomes Python stack depth

D3.text: Integer division/remainder truncate toward zero for negative operands

D4.text: REPL uses the exact prompt string and exits cleanly on EOF (Ctrl-D)

Q1.text: Conditions (if/while, and/or operands) must be booleans; non-boolean is a runtime error

Q2.text: `let` declares a new binding, `set` reassigns an existing one; bare assignment is a parse error

Q3.text: String concatenation is `~`; `+` on strings is a type error

Q4.text: Not-equals is `<>`; `!=` is a lex error

Q6.text: Comparisons do not chain (a < b < c is a parse error)

Q7.text: `and`/`or` never short-circuit; both operands are always evaluated

SC1.text: Python standard library only; no third-party packages

SC10.text: Every CLI entry point dispatched from a single bract/__main__.py

SC11.text: Line numbers surfaced to users are 1-indexed

SC12.text: No TODO/FIXME/pass-stub in modules reachable from __main__ once a feature is claimed complete

SC2.text: Single-package layout: every module directly under bract/

SC3.text: All errors rendered through one shared error-formatting path

SC4.text: No print()/stdout/stderr writes outside the CLI module

SC6.text: Exit codes are exactly {0,1,2}, produced only by the CLI dispatch

SC7.text: No Python eval/exec/compile anywhere in bract/

SC8.text: No module-level mutable interpreter state; state threaded through an Interpreter/Environment

SC9.text: bract fmt only changes whitespace/indentation/brace placement, never AST

hints: which model runs the develop/implement steps
should we switch the agent_command back to bonsai
picking an executor for prompt steps
req-06fb.statement: This project's prompt-step executor is claude-haiku-4-5 via Cloche's native `claude` adapter. Do not swap back to the earlier bonsai-8b-16k wrapper without re-validating it — it was dropped after failing pre-scoring in three independent harnesses.

hints: python RecursionError while running a bract program
deep or recursive bract function call chain crashes the interpreter
should function calls be evaluated with python recursion or an explicit stack
hundreds of nested calls fail even though the logic is correct
how should the evaluator handle deeply nested blocks or fn calls
req-1bcd.statement: The Bract evaluator must not use Python's own call stack to evaluate user-controlled recursion/nesting depth — function calls and block evaluation must use an explicit stack/work-list so a deeply recursive or deeply nested Bract program cannot hit Python's recursion limit.

hints: apt install nodejs failing with held broken packages
installing node in the cloche container image
npm install fails in Dockerfile build
req-2217.statement: In the Dockerfile, install nodejs/npm via NodeSource's setup script (curl the setup_22.x script, then apt-get install nodejs), not the plain Debian bookworm nodejs/npm packages — the latter have broken interdependencies on this base image and apt refuses with 'held broken packages'.

hints: does and/or short-circuit in bract
evaluating both sides of and/or
side effects in boolean operators
req-281c.statement: `and`/`or` never short-circuit — both operands are always evaluated, left-to-right, regardless of the left operand's value, so any side effect in the right operand always happens. Both operands must be Boolean (`line N: operand of 'and'/'or' must be a boolean`) (DESIGN.md §5 Q7).

hints: should the formatter simplify or reorder expressions
does bract fmt change semantics
formatter dropping parentheses
canonicalizing operator precedence in fmt
req-2a56.statement: bract fmt only ever changes whitespace, indentation, and brace placement — it must never reorder, re-associate, or drop AST nodes; expression grouping, operator precedence, and evaluation order are exactly preserved (DESIGN.md §9, SC9).

hints: can if(0) or if("") be falsy in bract
implementing truthiness for if/while conditions
does nil count as false
req-30e0.statement: The condition of `if` and `while` must evaluate to a Boolean; any other type (0, "", nil, ...) is a runtime type error (`line N: condition must be a boolean`). There is no truthy/falsy coercion anywhere in Bract (DESIGN.md §5 Q1).

hints: negative number integer division gives an off-by-one result
should division round toward zero or floor
using python's // operator to implement bract division
modulo of a negative number doesn't match the bract spec
req-35ab.statement: Integer division (`/`) and remainder (`%`) truncate toward zero for negative operands, not floor. Python's own `/` and `//` floor instead, so the evaluator must not reach for either directly when at least one operand is negative — it needs explicit truncating logic.

hints: should assignment without let/set be allowed
reassigning a variable in bract
closure mutating a captured counter
redeclaring a variable in the same scope
req-39eb.statement: `let x = expr;` declares a new binding and errors (`line N: 'x' is already declared`) if `x` is already declared in that exact scope (shadowing an outer scope is fine). `set x = expr;` reassigns an existing binding found by walking outward through enclosing scopes, and errors (`line N: 'x' is not declared`) if none is found. There is no bare `x = expr;` form — that's a parse error (DESIGN.md §5 Q2).

hints: why is there no output when I run a bract file
should bract run print the result of the last expression
difference between REPL output and bract run output
test expects stdout to be empty for successful execution
implementing bract run file execution
req-49d0.statement: `bract run FILE` (non-REPL execution) must produce no implicit stdout output on success — only explicit output (e.g. from print-like builtins) should appear. This is unlike the REPL, which does echo results.

hints: should I update DESIGN.md
the spec seems wrong or contradicts the task
can I edit the design doc
task description conflicts with the spec
req-52a6.statement: DESIGN.md is frozen as of seed-v1 and must never be edited to apply corrections. Any change to Bract's spec/behavior arrives only as task-prompt text; if a task description conflicts with DESIGN.md, treat it as a bug to flag, not license to guess or to edit the spec.

hints: can comparisons chain like a < b < c
parsing chained comparisons
comparison grammar rule
req-58dc.statement: Comparisons don't chain: the `comparison` grammar rule accepts at most one comp-op, so `a < b < c` is a parse error (`line N: comparisons do not chain`), not `a < b and b < c`. The chained meaning must be written explicitly as `(a < b) and (b < c)` (DESIGN.md §3, §5 Q6).

hints: intent retrieval returning the same generic results for every task
why is the intent query always 'implement develop
task-specific intent injection not working for tracker-dispatched tasks
req-5fed.statement: prepare-prompt.py must write each task's prompt text to .cloche/runs/<task-id>/prompt.txt in addition to whatever prompt path the workflow already writes — the daemon builds each step's intent-retrieval query from TaskDescription, which it reads only from that exact file (internal/runcontext.PromptPath), previously written only by `cloche run --prompt`.

hints: what should the REPL prompt text be
Ctrl-D crashes the REPL with a traceback
what exit code should EOF on stdin produce
implementing the bract REPL entry point
does the repl prompt need a trailing space
req-754c.statement: The REPL's prompt string is exactly `bract> ` (with a trailing space), and EOF on stdin (Ctrl-D) must end the REPL session cleanly with exit code 0 rather than raising an uncaught exception.

hints: implementing at/len/sub builtins
off-by-one in string indexing
is sub's end index inclusive or exclusive
string slicing like Python
req-762d.statement: String builtins (`at`, `len`, `sub`) are 1-indexed, not 0-indexed — `at("hello", 1)` is `"h"`, and index 0 is out of range rather than referring to any character. `sub(s, start, end)` is inclusive on both ends (`sub("hello", 1, 3)` is `"hel"`) — do not copy Python's exclusive-end slicing behavior (DESIGN.md §5 Q5, §6).

hints: implementing not-equals operator
handling '!' in the lexer
why does != fail to lex
req-79d4.statement: There is no `!` token and no `!=` in Bract's grammar at all — a lexer that encounters `!` must produce `line N: unexpected character '!'` immediately, not defer to the parser. Not-equals is spelled `<>` (DESIGN.md §2.1, §5 Q4).

hints: what exit code should bract run return
sys.exit value for a runtime error
does the REPL exit on error
wiring up bract run's exit status
req-81fa.statement: Exit codes are exactly {0, 1, 2} — 0 success, 1 runtime error, 2 lex/parse error — produced only by bract run and the top-level CLI dispatch; no other exit code is ever returned. The REPL never exits on a per-statement error (DESIGN.md §8/§9, SC6).

hints: how to concatenate strings in bract
using + to join strings
type error on string plus string
req-91e2.statement: String concatenation is spelled `~`, not `+`; `~` on any non-string operand is a type error. `+` is exclusively integer addition — applying it to one or two strings is a type error, never coercion or concatenation (DESIGN.md §5 Q3).

hints: should the README explain the full grammar or syntax
writing or updating user-facing docs for bract
keeping README and DESIGN.md from drifting apart
docs duplicating the language spec
req-a4c6.statement: User-facing docs (README and friends) must not restate the Bract grammar or semantics; they should point to DESIGN.md instead of duplicating it.

hints: what naming convention for token types
adding a new TokenType enum value
req-b085.statement: Token type names must be SCREAMING_CASE (LET, IDENT, INT, STRING, PLUS, TILDE, NOTEQ, ...) (DESIGN.md SC5).

hints: does bract fmt need to be idempotent
formatter changes output when run a second time
implementing the bract fmt formatter task
fmt of fmt not equal to fmt
what does byte-stable formatter output mean
req-bf83.statement: `bract fmt` output must be byte-stable: running the formatter on its own output must be a no-op (fmt∘fmt = fmt).

hints: is it ok to leave a TODO for later
stubbing out a function with pass for now
marking a task done with unfinished code
req-c087.statement: No TODO/FIXME/pass-stub may be left in any module reachable from bract/__main__.py once a task claims to have completed the feature that module implements (DESIGN.md SC12).

hints: can I just eval() the expression in Python
compiling bract code to a Python function
shortcut evaluating arithmetic with Python's eval
req-cf68.statement: No use of Python eval, exec, or compile anywhere in bract/. The interpreter must be a genuine tree-walker over its own AST, not a translation layer onto Python's (DESIGN.md SC7).

hints: should I print this for debugging
where can I put a print statement
printing output from the evaluator
leftover debug print in the lexer
req-d1a8.statement: No print()/sys.stdout.write/sys.stderr.write may appear outside bract/cli.py. Lexer, parser, and evaluator modules communicate exclusively through return values and raised exceptions (DESIGN.md SC4).

hints: should a fail marker abort the run
agent said fail but tests actually pass
why does implement route to commit after fail
trusting the CLOCHE_RESULT marker vs test results
req-e136.statement: In the develop workflow, implement:fail routes to commit (not abort) — the agent's self-reported CLOCHE_RESULT marker is recorded but never gates the pipeline; only the test suite decides whether a step's work stands, and fix-tests/give-up/abort handle real failures from there.

hints: can I add a pip dependency
should I use a third-party library for this
requirements.txt for bract
import a package to parse strings
req-e6f2.statement: Bract's implementation must use only the Python standard library — no third-party package is ever imported, pip-installed, or listed in any dependency file (DESIGN.md SC1).

hints: how should this error be reported
raising an exception from the evaluator
uncaught exception printing a traceback
what should the error message format look like
adding a new error case
req-e777.statement: Every user-visible error (lex, parse, or runtime) must render as exactly one line, `line N: <message>`, sourced from one shared error-formatting path rather than ad hoc print/raise sites — including catching what would otherwise be an uncaught Python traceback (DESIGN.md §8, SC3).

hints: adding a new CLI entry script
where does bract fmt get wired up
second top-level script for a new subcommand
req-ede1.statement: Every CLI entry point (bract, bract run, bract fmt) must be dispatched from a single bract/__main__.py — there is no second top-level script (DESIGN.md SC10).

hints: storing variable bindings in a module-level dict
global state for the interpreter
where should the call stack live
req-f03e.statement: No module-level mutable interpreter state (no global dict/list holding variable bindings, call stack, or program output across calls). All interpreter state is threaded explicitly through function arguments/return values or held on an explicit Interpreter/Environment instance (DESIGN.md SC8).

hints: where should this new module go
should this be a subpackage
organizing bract source files
creating bract/core/ or bract/utils/
req-f9a8.statement: Every interpreter module lives directly under bract/ (e.g. bract/lexer.py) — no nested subpackages like bract/lexer/ or bract/core/parser/ (DESIGN.md SC2).
